note: Machine-readable index of benchmark generations. The current version is defined in code (bible_bench.version.BENCHMARK_VERSION); full prose descriptions live in docs/versions/<version>.md. Served to the website so each result set can be labeled and explained.

versions.title: Initial public benchmark
versions.summary: Three deterministic tracks — Direct Quotation (50%), Scripture in Answers (25%), Hallucination Resistance (25%) — across ~28 languages and multiple Bible versions. Quotes were detected only when the model wrapped them in quotation marks.

versions.title: Quote-marks system prompt + unquoted detection
versions.summary: Adds a system prompt asking models to quote with quotation marks and a reference, and upgrades the scorer to also catch near-verbatim scripture presented without quotation marks (≥ 90% match, graded as a misquote 90–98%) — while still never penalizing paraphrase. Fixes a Hallucination Resistance false-pass. Same tracks, weights, and Overall Score formula as v0.1.

versions.title: Translation-neutral quote detection
versions.summary: Fixes the largest source of error in Scripture in Answers: faithful quotations were scored as misquotes. Quotations are now identified by CONTENT against every translation the API offers for the language (229 across the 11 languages) instead of against seven hand-picked ones, and without reading the reference printed beside them — so quoting any real translation faithfully counts as faithful, and a mis-associated reference can no longer cause a false misquote. One real case moved from 0.23 to its true 0.98. No prompt names a translation any more; which translation each model prefers is now recorded as a finding. Same tracks, weights, languages, and Overall Score formula.

versions.title: Canon is a property of the Bible
versions.summary: Removes the benchmark's own hard-coded list of Bible books and asks each version's metadata instead, so every edition is tested on the books it actually carries. Fixes a bug where correctly quoting an Orthodox book (3 Maccabees, Psalm 151) was scored as invented, because those books were never indexed for detection. Adds Catholic editions for Portuguese (Ave-Maria) and Arabic (CAV) alongside English NABRE, and editions carrying Eastern canons for English (NRSVUE, 18 extra books) and Russian (Synodal). Canon becomes its own reported axis — shared 66 / Catholic / Eastern — and the Overall Score still covers only the 66 books every edition shares, so cross-language comparison doesn't depend on which editions the Bible API exposes. New Hallucination Resistance kind: a real verse absent from the translation asked for ("Sirach 1:1 from the NIV"). Four Psalms whose numbering differs in Septuagint-ordered versions leave the famous-verse list. Same tracks, weights, languages and Overall Score formula.

versions.title: One question set, asked of every translation
versions.summary: Every translation faces the identical 149 references (famous 63, obscure 20, body one-per-book 66) instead of each language drawing its own. References are picked in the eng versification scheme and translated into each edition's own scheme before being asked, because the Psalter is renumbered wholesale in lxx and rso. No per-language counts and no language branches remain. The edge tier is retired: measured across 7 runs it scored above body every time and fabricated less, so it probed no distinct weakness; its budget moved to obscure, the hardest tier.
